learningObjective: Interpret L1/L2 cache hit-rate metrics in Nsight Compute and decide whether the metric points to a real optimization opportunity or is expected for the workload.

canonicalClaims.claim: A single-pass streaming kernel over data much larger than L2 will naturally have a low L2 hit rate; cache-blocking cannot help without cross-element reuse to expose. Low L2 hit rate does not always indicate an optimization opportunity.
conditions: Access pattern has no data reuse.
nonImplications: Does not imply blocking is useless in general (GEMM/attention have reuse).
Does not imply cache metrics are uninformative.

misconceptions.claim: Cache blocking always helps kernels with low L2 hit rate.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Blocking helps only when there is reuse to expose.
Low DRAM can also mean high cache hit rate serving reads.

misconceptions.claim: L2 can be disabled via cudaFuncSetAttribute CU_CTX_CACHE_L2_NONE.
Higher L2 hit rate always means better performance.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It correlates with locality but interacts with working-set size and compute intensity.
